the low-affinity receptor P75NTR for neurotrophins is regulated by 1,25-dihydroxyvitamine D3 in glioma cells and in the spinal cord in vivo.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1, 25-(OH) 2D3 does regulate P75Ntr mRNA expression in C6 glioblastoma cells but not primary astrocytes, and this regulation may be mediated through a region of the P75Ntr promoter between -610 and +860 bp from the translation initiation site.
1, 25-dihydroxyvitamind-3 does not regulate the expression of the high-affinity neurotrophic receptors (Trk A, B, C) but regulates the expression of P75NTr in C6 gliomas and spinal cord.
1, 25-dihydroxyvitamine D3 (1.25 (OH)2D) does not influence the mRNA levels of the full-length or truncated forms of TrkA, TrkB or TrkC in astrocytes and C6 glioma cell cultures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1, 25-(OH)D3 regulates P75NTR expression in C6 glioblastoma cells, and that 1,24-(OH)2-D3 may be a potential regulator of P75NTr in vivo. 1,24-OH-D3 is a major form of 1,24-25-D3 in the blood and in the brain.
1, 25-(OH)D3 does not affect neurotrophin receptors in primary cultures of rat cortical astrocytes and C6 glioma cell line.
1, 25-Dihydrovitamin D3 does not influence neurotrophin and their receptors expression in astrocytes but it increases low-affinity neurotrhopin receptor expression in C6 gliomas and in-vivo.
